citation: Sardarmehni, Anchieta and Levis (2022). Solid waste optimization life-cycle framework in Python (SwolfPy). Journal of Industrial Ecology. https://doi.org/10.1111/jiec.13236
description: The SwolfPy JIE benchmark publishes a worked municipal-solid-waste model accompanying the SwolfPy software article. The SwolfPy project evaluates global-warming potential for a hypothetical but realistic city, then optimises the treatment system to reduce that impact while meeting a 40 percent landfill-diversion target. Monte Carlo experiments examine sensitivity to uncertain inputs. The repository identifies the required input-data, process-model and main-package versions and links an archived release. Source and supporting model files are public and free under GPL-2.0. Coverage is one synthetic municipal treatment system, with no real-world city or observation period established in the README. It is therefore recorded as a model benchmark, not as a real-world case study. The pinned dependencies are old and may need an isolated environment; this review did not test whether current packages reproduce the published results. The reusable configuration supports waste-system optimisation and uncertainty studies using SwolfPy (model-swolfpy). The catalogue describes the parent package but does not identify this separate published benchmark configuration.
name: SwolfPy JIE municipal-waste benchmark
notes: G7 G7-0275. Prepared draft only. Metadata review on 2026-09-27; no models, data or archives downloaded. Related-resource comparisons are reviewer mappings, not tested interoperability.
